items.title: Javon Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 3, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Sure. What happens too, a lot of students reach out, they’ll send a text, “Professor how are you?”

ctx.x: Yeah. Let me return to the academic situation for a moment. I’m wondering if you’ve had an added role of trying to stay in touch with students and so forth, to just see how they’re doing and do you get a sense of how they’re being affected by this?

Sure. What happens too, a lot of students reach out, they’ll send a text, “Professor how are you?” I’ll get an email, thinking about you, and then obviously with the passing of some of the musicians I used to work with and had friendships with the students are aware of that so I get a lot of emails from them as well. It’s very interesting. They’re trying to figure this out, they’ll want to know what does their future look like for the fall for the university which we’re still in a holding pattern as this is…

schools, like Notre Dame, are starting pretty quickly, as early as they can in August, to try to get it all in before Thanksgiving. So that’s what they’re trying anyway. So again I try to case-by-case students that are thinking about coming to the University of Hartford, Jackie McLean Institute of Jazz, they’re interested to know what’s going on and obviously all I can let them know is what I receive from the university because I don’t really know. But you’re right, there’s a lot of questions from faculty, from…
